In the field's terms
Model parameter settings: every law input set by name on the command line, with defaults (no standard field term in the records)
Definition

A settings card that lets every law input bundle — T_K, dG_ATP, coins, push, held source, IAM-A line, D, eraser share and clean-up, conv, by_type, by_job — be set individually by name (--law-set KEY=VALUE), with defaults coming from the simulator's own law card (minicell.law_card); each value carries its own basis.
What it does

It supplies, or lets a user override, every numeric input the Law Sphere needs to build the predicted state against which a sample is judged, and the same inputs can then be fit or swept on saved counts.
Why the instrument needs it

The Law Sphere (instrument 17) measures how the cell is performing against the law by comparing measured fidelity, gain and level region by region to a state predicted from the energetics of maintenance in the sample's own cell mix. Building that predicted state requires values for T_K, dG_ATP, coins, push, held source, IAM-A line, D, eraser share and clean-up, conv, by_type and by_job, so this card exists to hold, or let someone override, those values.

By naming any law input on the command line as --law-set KEY=VALUE; anything not set takes its default from the simulator's law card (minicell.law_card). Its source_kind is recorded as 'setting with a default (a chain rule)', with basis 'rule (defaults from the simulator's law card; each value carries its own basis below)'.

It enters the error used by the Law Sphere as eps / (1 - share): the held error is obtained by dividing the restore error by one minus this share, so that deliberate erasure is separated from unmaintained loss. The Law Sphere judges how the cell is performing against the law's expected state; some losses are made on purpose by the eraser (TET), and the held error is eps = eps_restore / (1 - s), so the eraser's share by type enters that expected held error. In mature blood the share drops out; in stem and progenitor types it adds to the held error.
How it is obtained or computed

Computed as eps = eps_restore / (1 - s), where s is the eraser's share of held losses. It is obtained by being set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement (basis: 'measured in few types'). fields: How it works

Each unit (an island, or a block of 50 CpGs; 237,850 units) is read from molecules by IAM-A's rule; the law's expected point is built in the sample's own shares from the law's inputs (coin, two coins per restore, slow-write rule, write error, eraser, meter); 16 layers per unit, per job and whole: the angle between the sample and the law (Fisher-Rao), fidelity, hold against the law and against itself, kicks held, phi, coins per restore, Koide Q (a conjectured mapping), write against the law, and the hold alarm against each type's measured position.
Why

The other instruments compare with healthy cells; the Law Sphere compares with the physics, so it shows which part of the law the cell is failing (hold, write, eraser) rather than only that it departs.
Physics

IAM's Law (links 1, 1d, 2, 2b): the hold's derived values (held error 0.04454, odds 21.45, 3.066 kT, phi 0.1464) are the sphere's healthy points; each type's own level is measured and substituted, labelled as such.
Where the data comes from
The sample's molecules; the input card (every law input by name, defaults from the cell simulator's law card); the runtime reference (units, never-marked islands, type_positions_v1.json).
The numbers

Hold alarm against each type's measured position: 40 of 41 unseen healthy libraries within (jackknife floor). The level-side alarm reads 2.49 on a healthy library because the law's level point lacks each type's own level and the copy terms.
Method and standard
Fisher-Rao geometry (Rao 1945; Bhattacharyya 1943); exact binomial counting floor (a chain update); block jackknife over units (spread about four times plain counting).
Known-answer test
Known-answer run after a chain update (test library): 9 expected moves, nothing else; relay test: planted isolated loss raised the hold alarm z 0.09 -> 2.58.
Limits
(1) The level layer is incomplete (each type's own level and the copy terms). (2) Koide Q is a conjectured mapping. (3) Mixtures use a pooled loose share (caveat in the layer table).
Where the result goes
bundle development.law_sphere (layers, per job, whole, hold alarm); the Law Sphere page; the report.
Code
stage_law_sphere (reading, hold_alarm, CARD, LAYERS, fit, sweep, save_counts)
How to rebuild it
Read each unit by IAM-A's rule; build the law's point from the card in the sample's shares; compute the layers; floor by the exact binomial and a jackknife.
History
Dated entries in the development log (METHYLPHYS_DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md) and the instrument's development record.

questions: Is the Koide reading established physics?
No: it is a conjectured mapping, labelled so in every layer table; the sphere's established geometry is the Fisher-Rao angle.
What makes the Law Sphere different from the pipeline's other instruments?

The other instruments compare a sample against other healthy cells. The Law Sphere instead compares the sample against the state predicted by IAM's Law itself, so it can point to which part of the law is failing — the hold, the write, or the eraser — rather than just showing that the sample looks abnormal.
How many units of DNA does the Law Sphere actually score for one sample?
237,850 units, where each unit is either an island or a block of 50 CpGs, each read from the molecules by IAM-A's rule.
Does the Law Sphere treat a sample made of mixed cell types the same way as a pure cell-type sample?

No. For the 'hold vs self' reading, IAM-A does not supply a separate expected value for each cell type in a mixture, so the sphere falls back to one pooled value applied across the whole mix. That means this layer (and anything built from it, like coins per restore) is not a true reading of any single cell type in a mixture — the per-job layers should be used instead.
Which layers does the Law Sphere report for each unit?

The angle between the sample and the law (Fisher-Rao distance) with its fidelity; the hold against the law and against the sample's own line; kicks held; the share of each coin kept as hold; coins per restore; the Koide balance (a conjectured mapping); writes against the law; and the hold alarm against each cell type's measured healthy level. Each is given per unit, per job and for the whole sample (16 layers in all).
